links.outcome: Reading level of ChatGPT responses (FKGL and FRES)
links.effect: Mean FKGL 7.8 ± 1.267 and mean FRES 52.68 ± 8.6; estimated reading level required was 'high school'.
links.quote: The mean FKGL score was 7.8 ± 1.267, and the mean FRES was 52.68 ± 8.6.

links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT musculoskeletal responses for patients
links.effect: Mean FKGL 7.8 and FRES 52.68; average estimated reading level was high school, above plain-language targets.
links.quote: The average estimated reading level required to understand the text was considered as "high school".

links.outcome: Expert Likert ratings of diagnosis, recommendation, and referral accuracy of ChatGPT responses
links.effect: Most responses rated adequate or excellent; diagnosis scores differed by area of interest (p = 0.007), attributed to trauma-related questions; no significant difference in other categories.
links.quote: However, in the diagnosis category, a significant difference was found in the evaluation made according to the AoI (p = 0.007), which is attributed to trauma-related questions.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates the reliability, comprehensibility, and readability of ChatGPT 4.0 outputs for orthopaedic patient queries (musculoskeletal disorders) via expert ratings and readability metrics, but does not test a specific deployment practice or guardrail.
